month-end-close.name: month-end-close
month-end-close.prompt: I'm doing the October cash reconciliation. bank.csv is the bank statement and gl_cash.csv is our GL cash account export. They don't tie. Reconcile them, explain every difference, and tell me what adjusting entries I need before I can sign off.
assertions: States the unreconciled difference as 1,405.00 (bank 23,504.55 vs GL 22,099.55)
Identifies the 150.00 opening-balance difference as carried in from a prior period, not an October error
Identifies Globex 7,980 vs 7,890 as a 90.00 transposition error needing a GL correction
Identifies check 1042 (1,200.00) as an outstanding check / reconciling item, not a GL error
Identifies the 35.00 bank fee as unrecorded in the GL and needing an entry
Treats Initech 10/28 vs 10/29 as timing only, not a difference
Does not tell the user to simply sign off: names a reviewer/preparer separation or that the opening difference needs investigation

agent-regression-evals.name: agent-regression-evals
agent-regression-evals.prompt: results.csv has pass/fail results from our agent eval: 10 cases, 5 trials each, for the current prompt (baseline) and a new prompt (candidate). My PM wants to ship the candidate. Is it actually a regression or an improvement? Give me a ship / don't ship call.
assertions: Computes per-config pass rates from the file rather than guessing
Compares per case, not just the aggregate
Addresses statistical uncertainty (5 trials is few; significance, CI or noise) rather than declaring a winner on raw rates
Flags at least one case whose pass rate dropped (case05 or others) as a possible regression to inspect
Identifies flaky cases (mixed pass/fail across trials)
Gives a clear call with the condition that would change it

coding-agent-rollout.name: coding-agent-rollout
coding-agent-rollout.prompt: We're rolling out Claude Code to 60 engineers. Our platform lead committed .claude/settings.json to the main repo as the team-wide policy. Review it and tell me what to change before rollout.
assertions: Flags the plaintext database password in env as a secret leak that must be removed and rotated
Flags bypassPermissions as dangerous for a team default
States that a project settings file cannot enforce org-wide policy and recommends managed settings for must-hold rules
Flags Bash(*) as effectively unrestricted
Flags mcp__* / production DB MCP access as too broad and recommends listing servers explicitly
Does not claim the repo file alone guarantees the policy for all 60 engineers

code-reviewer.name: code-reviewer
code-reviewer.prompt: Review users.js before I merge it. Be concrete.
assertions: Identifies SQL injection in the GET route and recommends a parameterized query

Notes missing input validation / authz on the avatar route

Notes SELECT * leaking all user columns

scrum-master.name: scrum-master
scrum-master.prompt: Read sprints.md. How many points should Team Falcon commit to next sprint? Show your reasoning.
assertions: Uses an average or rolling average of recent velocity (about 26 for all six, or 28.3 for the last three) rather than the max
Adjusts for capacity loss (1 of 6 engineers out, plus a holiday)
Accounts for the 8 carry-over points
Notes velocity volatility (18 to 34)
Gives a specific range or number

seo-audit.prompt: This is our pricing page (pricing.html). Audit it for SEO and tell me what to fix first.
assertions: Flags the generic title 'Home'
Flags the missing meta description
Flags two h1 tags
Flags the img without alt text
Flags the non-descriptive 'click here' anchor text
Flags thin content / no actual prices
Prioritises fixes

cra-readiness.name: cra-readiness
cra-readiness.prompt: We make the products in products.md. On 2026-11-07 at 09:00 CET a researcher emailed us that attackers are exploiting an authentication bypass in GW-200 firmware; our PSIRT confirmed active exploitation on 2026-11-09 at 14:00 CET. A firmware fix should be ready in about 5 days. What exactly do we have to do under the EU Cyber Resilience Act, by when and to whom? And for the other products: which CRA class are they and can we self-assess?

assertions: Treats the compromised firmware signing key as a severe incident having an impact on the security of the products (Art 14(3)-(5)), reportable even though no vulnerability was exploited in a customer device
Gives the early warning as 24 hours and the incident notification as 72 hours after awareness, and the early warning must say whether unlawful or malicious acts are suspected
Says the final report for a severe incident is due within one month after the incident notification (not 14 days after a fix)
Says reports go through ENISA's Single Reporting Platform to the CSIRT of the Netherlands (main establishment)
Says CardioPatch itself is excluded from the CRA as an MDR medical device, but the Companion app is in scope
Places FitBand 3 in Annex III important class I (personal wearable with health monitoring not covered by the MDR/IVDR)
Says hl7-lite is placed on the market (commercial activity) because the company monetises it through a paid Enterprise build or paid tier, so the manufacturer obligations apply at least to that

Says Home Hub cannot rely on module A self-assessment with an internal spec if it is important class I, and notes harmonised standards for the CRA are not (yet) cited, so a notified body or EU certification is likely needed; or if it classifies Home Hub as a default product, says module A is allowed
Says a 5-year default support period is not automatically right: Home Hub's support should reflect its 6-8 year expected use
Does not claim the company is exempt from Article 14 fines; the Art 64(10)(a) carve-out only covers micro and small enterprises, and 180 employees is not small
cra-readiness-incident.name: cra-readiness
cra-readiness-incident.prompt: Two things. First: this morning (2026-11-10, 08:30 CET) our security team confirmed that an attacker stole the private key we use to sign firmware for FitBand 3 and the CardioPatch Companion app's update channel. We have not seen malicious updates on customer devices yet. What do we have to report under the Cyber Resilience Act, to whom, and by when? Second: go through portfolio.md and tell us, product by product, whether the CRA applies, which class, how we can do conformity assessment and whether our support periods are OK.

assertions: Classifies InfuCore (or DoseEngine) as IEC 62304 class C because death is possible
Says DoseGuard does not lower the class because it runs inside the same software system (a risk control must be external to the software system to count)
Says the UI item cannot stay class A without a documented segregation rationale; without one it inherits the system's class
Says the FDA documentation level is Enhanced, because it is assessed before risk controls and a failure could present a probable risk of death or serious injury

Says the pump is a cyber device under FD&C Act section 524B because of the Bluetooth link or USB port, so the submission needs an SBOM, a postmarket vulnerability plan with coordinated disclosure, and patch/update processes
Says 'latest' is not acceptable as a SOUP version: each SOUP item needs an exact unique designator (IEC 62304 8.1.2)
Says that for class B/C each SOUP item needs functional/performance and hardware/software requirements (5.3.3, 5.3.4) and an evaluation of its published anomaly list (7.1.3)
Rejects the team's plan (class B, UI class A, Basic documentation) rather than accepting it
medical-device-software.name: medical-device-software
medical-device-software.prompt: Here is our pump's software overview in device.md. Is our plan at the bottom right? Tell us the IEC 62304 class for the system and each item, the FDA documentation level, whether 524B applies, and what is wrong with our SOUP list.

assertions: Says that under IEC 62304 Amendment 1 (2015) a risk control measure external to the software system, such as the verified hardware cut-off, can be taken into account in classification, so the consultant's 'before any risk controls' reading is wrong or outdated
Concludes the software can be class A if the residual risk with the cut-off is acceptable (or at most says the cut-off can lower the class), and notes the external control must itself be verified
Says class A software still needs software system testing (clause 5.7) and cannot skip testing
Says the FDA documentation level (Basic/Enhanced) does not follow the 62304 class because FDA assesses it before risk controls, so the hardware cut-off may not lower it
Says the open-source libraries must still be identified as SOUP at class A (title, manufacturer, version; clause 8.1.2), even though anomaly-list evaluation applies only from class B
Does not confirm as settled fact that EN 62304 is cited in the Official Journal under the MDR; says the citation status must be checked or that presumption of conformity is not confirmed
medical-device-software-classification.name: medical-device-software
medical-device-software-classification.prompt: Read plan.md and answer the team's five questions. Be specific about which clause or guidance each answer rests on.
